Definition: {to hear intelligently (often with implication of attention, obedience, etc.; causatively, to tell, etc.)}
BiblicalUsage: To hear, in Daniel's Aramaic, is usually to hear music and obey it. At what time ye hear the sound of the cornet and flute and harp, ye fall down and worship the golden image: hearing is the trigger for idolatry. But Belshazzar says he has heard of Daniel, that he can dissolve doubts, and the kingdom is promised to the people who shall hear and obey the Most High.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe hearing is never neutral in Daniel. The same ears that hear the music and bow to the image can hear of Daniel and seek the truth, and I hold that what we do with what we hear is the whole test.
